word_ladder_ii.brute:
if endWord not in wordList: return []
best = []
all_paths(word, path):   (DFS over every simple path from beginWord)
    if word == endWord:
        if best is empty or path is shorter than best[0]: clear best
        if best is empty or path is as long as best[0]: append a copy of path to best
        return
    for each candidate in wordList:   (neighbours by comparing every word)
        if candidate not in path and candidate differs from word in exactly one letter:
            all_paths(candidate, path + [candidate])
all_paths(beginWord, [beginWord])
return best

bus_routes.brute:
if source == target: return 0
adjacent[i] = every other route j that shares a stop with route i   (test every pair of routes)
queue = deque of (i, 1) for every route i containing source; seen = those routes
while the queue is not empty:
    (route, buses) = pop from the front
    if target is on route: return buses
    for each other in adjacent[route] not in seen:
        add other to seen, push (other, buses + 1) to the back
return -1

jump_game_iv.optimal:
if n == 1: return 0
indices_of = dict value -> list of every index holding it
seen = all false, seen[0] = true; queue = deque of [0]; jumps = 0
while the queue is not empty:
    for each index currently in the queue:   (one layer = one jump)
        i = pop from the front
        if i == n - 1: return jumps
        neighbours = [i - 1, i + 1]
        if arr[i] in indices_of:
            add indices_of[arr[i]] to neighbours, then delete it   (all of this value is queued now: never rescan)
        for each j in neighbours:
            if j in bounds and not seen[j]: seen[j] = true, push j to the back
    jumps += 1
return -1

shortest_path_in_a_grid_with_obstacles_e.brute:
obstacles = list of every cell with grid value 1
steps_avoiding(cleared) = plain BFS from (0, 0) over 0 cells and cleared cells; steps to the corner or -1
best = -1
for each size from 0 to min(k, number of obstacles):
    for each subset of obstacles of that size:   (a full BFS for every subset)
        steps = steps_avoiding(set of subset)
        if steps != -1 and (best == -1 or steps < best): best = steps
return best

shortest_path_to_get_all_keys.brute:
position = dict symbol -> cell for '@' and every key; keys = the key letters sorted
moves_between(start, goal, held) = BFS over cells skipping walls and locks whose key is not held; -1 if cut off
best = -1
for each permutation order of keys:   (the same (cell, keys held) is searched again and again)
    total = 0, current = position['@'], held = empty set
    for each key in order:
        leg = moves_between(current, position[key], held)
        if leg == -1: total = -1, stop this order
        total += leg, current = position[key], add key to held
    if total != -1 and (best == -1 or total < best): best = total
return best
shortest_path_to_get_all_keys.optimal:
all_keys = bitmask with one bit per key on the grid; start = (row of '@', col of '@', 0)
queue = deque of [start], seen = {start}, moves = 0
while the queue is not empty:
    for each state currently in the queue:   (one layer = one move)
        (row, col, held) = pop from the front
        if held == all_keys: return moves
        for each direction:
            new_held = keys after entering the neighbour cell: -1 if out of bounds, a wall, or a lock without its key
                       held with the key's bit set if the cell is a key, else held
            state = (neighbour row, neighbour col, new_held)
            if new_held != -1 and state not in seen:   (same cell, more keys: a new state)
                add state to seen, push it to the back
    moves += 1
return -1

shortest_path_visiting_all_nodes.brute:
distance[a] = plain BFS distances from a to every node, for each node a   (all-pairs)
best = -1
for each permutation order of the n nodes:   (n! orders; shared prefixes are redone)
    total = 0
    for each i from 0 to n - 2: total += distance[order[i]][order[i + 1]]
    if best == -1 or total < best: best = total
return best
shortest_path_visiting_all_nodes.optimal:
if n == 1: return 0
everyone = bitmask with all n bits set
queue = deque of (node, 1 << node, 0) for every node; seen = set of (node, 1 << node)   (start anywhere)
while the queue is not empty:
    (node, visited, length) = pop from the front
    for each neighbour of node:
        new_visited = visited with bit neighbour set
        if new_visited == everyone: return length + 1
        if (neighbour, new_visited) not in seen:   (a node may repeat, a state may not)
            add (neighbour, new_visited) to seen, push (neighbour, new_visited, length + 1) to the back
return -1

parallel_courses_iii.brute:
finish = copy of time   (a course with no prerequisite ends at time[c])
changed = true
while changed:   (at most n sweeps, each over every relation)
    changed = false
    for each (prev, nxt) in relations:
        candidate = finish[prev] + time[nxt]
        if candidate > finish[nxt]: finish[nxt] = candidate, changed = true
return max of finish
parallel_courses_iii.optimal:
unlocks[c] = courses that need c first; in_degree[c] = number of prerequisites of c
finish = copy of time   (no prerequisites -> ends at time[c])
queue = deque of every course with in_degree == 0
while the queue is not empty:   (Kahn's topological order)
    course = pop from the front   (finish[course] is final: every prerequisite was popped already)
    for each nxt in unlocks[course]:
        finish[nxt] = max(finish[nxt], finish[course] + time[nxt])
        in_degree[nxt] -= 1
        if in_degree[nxt] == 0: push nxt to the back
return max of finish
